data: The discovery of radioactivity opened up a whole new realm of physics beyond the classical gravitational and electromagnetic interactions. The properties and structure of the nucleus within an atom, and the forces that bind their constituent protons and neutrons together will be discussed in this course. Using the basic tools of quantum mechanics and special relativity, one can understand the phenomena of alpha, beta and gamma decay, and radioactive transmutations. Even more fundamental than protons and neutrons are the elementary particles -- quarks, leptons and the bosons that mediate interactions between them. Their description as given by the Standard Model of particle physics will be introduced. Finally, the course will discuss detectors and experimental techniques relevant for nuclear and particle physics.
